datasets.name: LIBERO-PeRM
datasets.description: A benchmark for personalized robotic manipulation, comprising five task suites and 312 preference-conditioned tasks with 40.8k demonstrations.

datasets.name: LIBERO-SinglePref
datasets.description: A task suite within LIBERO-PeRM for evaluating single-preference learning (100 tasks).

datasets.name: LIBERO-PrefScale
datasets.description: A task suite within LIBERO-PeRM for evaluating scaling across data sizes, tasks, and layouts (100 tasks).

datasets.name: LIBERO-PrefConflict
datasets.description: A task suite within LIBERO-PeRM for evaluating preference-preference and task-preference conflicts (48 tasks).

datasets.name: LIBERO-PrefCompose
datasets.description: A task suite within LIBERO-PeRM for evaluating multi-preference composition (64 tasks).

datasets.name: LIBERO-ComprePref
datasets.description: A task suite within LIBERO-PeRM for evaluating realistic preference-conditioned reasoning based on contextual language.

metrics.name: Preference-satisfaction metrics
metrics.description: Metrics used to evaluate how well user preferences are met.

metrics.name: Task success
metrics.description: A general metric for evaluating task completion.

concepts.name: Personalization
concepts.description: The requirement for embodied agents to execute tasks aligning with user preferences, habits, and constraints.

concepts.name: Personalized Robotic Manipulation (PeRM)
concepts.description: Robotic manipulation that satisfies user-specific constraints on strategies and actions.

concepts.name: Preferences
concepts.description: User-specific constraints on how actions are performed or strategies are selected for identical goals.

concepts.name: Observable preferences in simulation
concepts.description: A controlled taxonomy of preferences covering motion, skill, and user-profile choices, restricted to language-expressible, automatically evaluable, and reusable preferences.

concepts.name: Motion Preference
concepts.description: A type of preference that constrains the physical properties of a trajectory.

concepts.name: Skill Preference
concepts.description: A type of preference that alters the execution behavior of a specific skill.

concepts.name: User Profile
concepts.description: A type of preference that uses background knowledge (user profile/context) to guide subtask-level semantic choices.

concepts.name: Zero-shot personalization
concepts.description: The ability of policies to follow preferences without preference data.

concepts.name: Single preference learning
concepts.description: The ability of policies to learn individual preferences from demonstrations.

concepts.name: Learning efficiency
concepts.description: How efficiently policies acquire preferences as demonstrations increase.

concepts.name: Preference generalization
concepts.description: How learned preferences generalize across layouts and tasks.

concepts.name: Preference composition and conflict handling
concepts.description: How policies compose multiple preferences and behave under conflicts.

concepts.name: Household manipulation
concepts.description: A long-standing goal in robotics and embodied AI.

concepts.name: Embodied AI
concepts.description: A field related to robots operating in physical environments.

concepts.name: Generalist robotic manipulation
concepts.description: Robotic manipulation that generalizes across diverse inputs and embodiments.

concepts.name: Cross-embodiment generalization
concepts.description: The ability of a robot policy to work across different robot bodies.

concepts.name: Generalized manipulation
concepts.description: Broad manipulation capabilities.

concepts.name: Long-horizon reasoning
concepts.description: The ability to plan and execute complex, multi-step tasks.

concepts.name: Sim-to-real transfer
concepts.description: The ability to transfer policies learned in simulation to real-world robots.

concepts.name: Lifelong learning
concepts.description: The ability of a system to continuously learn over its lifetime.

concepts.name: Task generalization
concepts.description: The ability of a policy to perform well on new, unseen tasks.

concepts.name: Implicit preference alignment
concepts.description: A way personalization is defined in some prior work, often via human feedback or reward signals.

concepts.name: Multi-user style adaptation
concepts.description: A way personalization is defined in some prior work, adapting to different user styles.

concepts.name: User-specific object-receptacle pairing
concepts.description: A way personalization is defined in some prior work, involving specific object-receptacle choices.

concepts.name: Helpful action prediction
concepts.description: A way personalization is defined in some prior work, predicting actions that are helpful to users.

concepts.name: Subtask decompositions
concepts.description: Breaking down a task into smaller, manageable subtasks.

concepts.name: Subgoal-image annotations
concepts.description: Images associated with specific subgoals within a task.

findings.name: Current VLA policies struggle with zero-shot personalization
findings.description: Experiments show that current Vision-Language-Action policies have difficulty following preferences in zero-shot settings.

findings.name: SFT makes preferences learnable
findings.description: Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) is effective in enabling policies to learn preferences.

findings.name: Mixed training achieves better no-preference retention than sequential adaptation
findings.description: A mixed training approach maintains better performance on tasks without preferences compared to sequential adaptation.

findings.name: Mixed training improves performance with contextual prompts compared with preference-only training
findings.description: Mixed training, when combined with contextual prompts, leads to better task success and preference satisfaction than preference-only LoRA.

findings.name: Mixed training can weaken motion-preference learning
findings.description: While beneficial in some aspects, mixed training may negatively impact the learning of motion preferences.

findings.name: Broader layout diversity and matched no-preference data help
findings.description: Increasing the diversity of layouts and providing corresponding no-preference data improves performance.

findings.name: Preference generalization, decomposition, and conflict handling remain difficult
findings.description: The ability of learned preferences to generalize, decompose, and be handled under conflicts is still challenging for current policies.
